ticket.title: Root the telemetry writer at the suite and delete the federating reader
ticket.description: Reverse the compensation. The flight recorder resolves the canonical directory of the working directory, so a suite of twelve repositories has twelve logs; the panel resolved one path from its own working directory, showed nothing, and GB-293 answered by writing a reader that enumerates every member log (telemetry_event_paths) instead of moving the writer. That reader was committed to benchwork-core and is never called, and the daemon still tails a single path (routes_telemetry.rs:58). Root the writer at the declared suite via Membership::containing on a canonicalised path, the canonicalisation being what GB-327 lost a session to, falling back to the repository root when no suite lists it. Delete telemetry_event_paths and the multi-tail. Telemetry is derived and untracked, so it centralises: there is nothing to merge and worktrees already share it through the common dir. Delete the stale sawhorse telemetry log rather than migrating it, and record in the ADR why it existed and why it is gone, so a future reader can tell never-used from deliberately-retired.
acceptance_criteria: one log per suite; a run inside a member writes to the suite root and says so on stderr; no code path enumerates member logs; the stale sawhorse log is gone with an ADR paragraph explaining the before and after

events.description:
Reverse the compensation. The flight recorder resolves the canonical directory of the working directory, so a suite of twelve repositories has twelve logs; the panel resolved one path from its own working directory, showed nothing, and GB-293 answered by writing a reader that enumerates every member log (telemetry_event_paths) instead of moving the writer. DONE 2026-11-08, three commits, one per repository.

common b206df0: gaugeblock_workspace::sink_path resolves the declared suite first (canonicalised before asking
membership, the GB-327 lesson) and falls back to the repository when no suite lists the caller. Three tests: member ->
suite root, lone checkout -> its own directory, outside a checkout -> no sink.
sawhorse d6c1f07: the one emitter writes to sink_path instead of resolving its own working directory. The stale
sawhorse telemetry log is deleted rather than migrated - it held two unit-test artifacts, which GB-340 made
impossible, and moving them would have carried junk into the log that replaces them.
benchwork f55cf7f: telemetry_paths and its tests are deleted. It was the compensation for a writer that resolved one
directory, and it was committed here and never called - so removing it removes a plan, not a feature.

One test failed first for an instructive reason: the lone-checkout case built an empty .git directory, which is not a
repository because Repository::discover asks git. It now runs a real git init.

Still owed in the telemetry set: GB-339 (one span per CLI invocation across nine more tools, the epic), GB-341
(retention with tracked aggregates), SP-2 ([telemetry] enabled, the config half of ADR 0012).
